source.title: CADENCE: A Cardiac Atom Dictionary for Interpretable Neural Concept Extraction from ECG Foundation Models
source.authors: Yi-Xuan Duan; Arjun Naik; Sadeer Al-Kindi; Weijing Qiu

record.tranche_reason: The study compares concept selectivity of an ECG model’s dense dimensions, described as raw neurons, with SAE atoms, and argues that the atoms are more concept-aligned. It does not measure the fraction of neuron poles with one or two jobs, but its results challenge the broader claim that individual neurons are the appropriate interpretable units.
record.gate_note: The study does not audit Qwen3-32B or estimate the share of neuron poles with one or two jobs. Its direct evidence is about concept association of dense dimensions versus SAE atoms in an ECG model. It also tests atom ablations and held-out atom-description predictions; these are reported below as related findings, not as tests of the listed claims about neurons.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It assumes neurons are polysemantic and in superposition, citing prior work, and builds SAE atoms on that premise. Its dense-versus-atom comparison uses residual-stream coordinates of a 6-layer ECG transformer. These are not MLP neuron poles, and the study gives no share of units with one or two jobs, no LLM or scale comparison, no InceptionV1 analysis, no neuron-based attribution graphs, and no scoring of neuron explanations. The best-dimension AUROC comparison and the LLM scoring of SAE atoms measure related but different constructs.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also frame atoms as evidence that ECG embeddings store concepts in superposition and are monosemantically decomposable. They describe atom ablations as showing that atoms are functional units.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a BatchTopK sparse autoencoder on frozen ECG foundation-model residual-stream activations, then evaluates clinical concept association, atom ablation, and LLM-generated atom descriptions. It does not use the Qwen neuron-pole audit or its one-job/two-job/unknown categorization.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer changes concept association: results improve with depth from Layer 1 to Layer 6. SAE dictionary size and sparsity were selected by grid search; at Layer 6 the chosen configuration was F = 8192 and k = 128. Atom descriptions were assessed on a filtered subset of interpretable atoms.

fits_no_version.finding: In a frozen ECG transformer, the best SAE atom per concept has higher held-out AUROC than the best residual-stream dimension: Layer 6 phenotype 0.88 vs 0.78, morphology 0.90 vs 0.83, and PTB-XL 0.825 vs 0.720. The gap widens with depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In an ECG foundation model, SAE atoms are more concept-selective than individual residual-stream dimensions.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the target-associated SAE atom lowers a frozen linear readout's target logit (−0.27 to −0.62). Random and other-concept atom controls leave it unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selected SAE atoms in an ECG model act as selective units for downstream linear readouts.

fits_no_version.finding: LLM descriptions of 1000 sampled filtered ECG SAE atoms predict held-out activations with median Spearman ρ 0.65; 92% exceed 0.3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automated descriptions of pre-filtered ECG SAE atoms predict held-out activation rank well.

record.peer_reviewed: KDD ’27 (Proceedings of the 33rd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; as stated in the text)
record.problems: The paper does not quantify how many original neurons have one or more jobs. Diagnostic phenotype labels include keyword matching on machine reports, and report enrichment shares its source with labels. The study notes that atom naming may be incomplete and limited by fixed geometric heuristics. Only 1000 of 2991 eligible atoms were included in the automated description evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported concept-by-concept values from Table A1 were extracted; the aggregate Layer-6 comparisons and across-layer summary capture the relevant dense-dimension versus atom results. No rows were added for model prediction probes, because those compare prediction performance rather than how many units have one main job.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or neuron-pole job shares.
No language models, dense/MoE comparison or scaling.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron reanalysis.
No test of architecture, regularization or tools as causes of messy neurons. No interpretable-neuron share estimates.
No attribution graphs built from model neurons. Interventions use SAE atoms, a replacement basis.
No test of neuron explanations from activating examples failing to predict firing.
No simulation scoring of neuron explanations. Only filtered SAE atoms are scored.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T5/tests guess is wrong. The dense baseline is residual-stream coordinates, which lack a privileged basis, not MLP neurons; the study never audits neurons. Only 2991 of 8192 atoms passed the pre-filter for automated description, and lead-diffuse atoms were excluded after a pilot showed they failed validation. Table A1 shows dense units beating atoms for some concepts in early layers, such as atrial flutter at L1.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or estimate of the proportions of neuron poles with one job, two related jobs, or an unknown job.
No language-model, dense/MoE scaling comparison or assessment up to trillions of parameters.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or test of pose detection, recursive generalization, or superposition in that example.
No test of architecture or regularization as the cause of messy late-layer neurons, or estimates of interpretability shares for InceptionV1-sized vision models.

The study ablates SAE atoms and reads a frozen predictor; it does not test whether attribution graphs built from the model’s own neurons explain behavior without a replacement model and its reconstruction error.
No test of explanations written from activating examples that fail to predict where a neuron fires.
The study scores LLM descriptions of ECG SAE atoms on held-out ECG activations, not explanations of neurons on new text.

rows.subject: CSFM (Cardiac Sensing FM), Tiny variant
rows.operation_detail: Compared the best single SAE-atom AUROC with the best dense-embedding dimension AUROC for phenotype concepts.
rows.note: The study reports greater concept association for an SAE atom than for a dense dimension, but this AUROC comparison does not estimate the fraction of neurons with a single main job.
rows.check: Baseline is a residual-stream coordinate, not an MLP neuron. A best-dimension AUROC cannot show what share of neurons have one job.

rows.note: This compares feature selectivity, not the percentage of dense dimensions that have one nameable job.
rows.check: Same as r1: residual-stream dimension, best-unit selectivity, not a neuron-share audit.

rows.subject: CSFM (Cardiac Sensing FM), Tiny variant
